issues.description: Resolver.resolve() postcondition silently weakened: returned requirements are no longer marked prepared.
issues.detail: The deleted block in resolver.py used to set req.prepared = True and needs_more_preparation = False. Now resolve() returns a half-prepared set and the obligation is shifted to every caller without docstring or assertion. Any extension, test, or future command consuming RequirementSet inherits inconsistent state. Document the new contract on resolve() or restore the flag flip.

issues.description: set_dist/get_dist caches a metadata-only distribution with no invalidation after the full download.
issues.detail: _fetch_metadata_only stores a metadata-only BaseDistribution in self._distribution. get_dist() returns it in preference to metadata_directory and local_file_path, so even after prepare_linked_requirements_more downloads the real wheel the stale cache wins. RECORD/file-list divergence becomes silent wrong behavior. Invalidate _distribution on full prep or document the precedence.

issues.description: prepare_linked_requirements_more is copy-pasted across three commands instead of a shared helper.
issues.detail: download.py, install.py, and wheel.py each grew the identical post-resolve call. A fourth command (pip lock, the very motivation cited) will forget it. Either push the call back into resolve() behind a dry_run flag or extract one finish_preparation helper. Sprinkling the same incantation across call sites is not decoupling.

issues.description: set_dist/get_dist introduced with no specification, invariants, or precedence documentation.
issues.detail: set_dist is a one-line setter with no docstring, no validation, no statement of when it is valid to call. get_dist now has a four-branch if/elif ladder (_distribution, metadata_directory, local_file_path+is_wheel, editable) with implicit priority. Either give the cache an enforced invariant and documented precedence, or collapse to a single canonical dist field.

issues.description: download_info backfill inside _fetch_metadata_only mixes two concerns and may break on dry-run with VCS URLs.
issues.detail: prepare_linked_requirement now both fetches metadata and synthesizes download_info as a side effect via direct_url_from_link(req.link, req.source_dir), guarded only by 'if download_info is None'. In dry-run req.source_dir may not exist, which works in CI but explodes on VCS URLs. Either return both values explicitly or set download_info at the single site that needs it.

issues.description: No test asserts that --dry-run actually avoids downloading the full wheel.
issues.detail: The headline behavior is 'dry-run no longer fetches wheel bytes when PEP-658 metadata is available'. The diff moves calls around but ships no test that fails before the patch and passes after. A small integration test with a mock index that errors on wheel GET would pin the contract; without it a future refactor silently re-introduces the download.

synthesis.summary: The panel agrees the direction is correct — eager full-download inside resolve() was the bug and deferring final preparation to commands is the right fix. But the execution silently weakens Resolver.resolve()'s postcondition, copy-pastes the replacement call across three commands instead of one helper, and introduces a set_dist/get_dist cache with no invalidation when the real download later lands. Contracts for the new boundary are undocumented and the download_info backfill entangles two concerns with a fragile source_dir assumption. Ship-blockers: document or restore the resolver contract, invalidate the metadata-only dist on full prep, consolidate the call site, and add a test that proves no wheel is fetched under --dry-run.
